newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Salmon minimum import prices seen unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Salmon minimum import prices seen unlikely.

text.p: The European Commission is unlikely to agree to a British request to impose minimum prices on imports of farmed salmon, Commission officials said on Wednesday.

Britain made the request at the Fisheries Council on November 22 following complaints from Scottish producers that Norwegian salmon was being dumped onto the EU market at below cost price and had depressed the market.
"The Commission is sceptical of the efficiency of minimum import prices," said one official, noting that there were numerous ways of cheating.

Minimum import prices applied during the first half of 1996 had little success in stabilising prices and were accepted by processing countries, such as Denmark, as a "one-off" measure, the official added.

Another official said that even if the Commission agreed after consultations with member states to introduce minimum import prices, it would be too late to have any impact before the end of year holidays when salmon demand peaks.
Officials noted that the Commission was investigating a complaint against the dumping of Norwegian salmon onto the EU market and this would not be completed until May 1997.
The Commission's fisheries spokesman cautioned that nothing had been decided.
"No decision has been taken. The Commissioner is assessing the grounds for any action," Filippo di Robilant told Reuters.
